Be sure the Robot Odyssey I
disk is in the drive.

Then press ESC.

To go back to the room you
just left, press RETURN.

INNOVATION LAB Chip Functions


 BURN:    Wire prototype. Position
          chips in Burner Room.
          Activate burn button.

 SAVE:    Pick up chip. Press S.

 LOAD:    Pick up chip. Press L.

 RECORD:  Pick up chip. Press ?.

Press P to become the Paintbrush.

Press C to become the Cursor.

a circuit inside.
To continue, press RETURN.

Shape Editor

Welcome! Here you will learn
about things you can do in the
INNOVATION LAB. You'll learn
how to use the:

If you don't know ROBOT ANATOMY
and TOOLKIT, press ESC and
return to the menu.

This is a 
PROTOTYPE CHIP.
It has 8 pins that
can be soldered
to wires.

Notice how the
pins are numbered.

The pins on this chip are neither
outputs nor inputs because the 
chip isn't wired.
Take the chip with you.

This circuit sends out
pulses of electricity.
Go inside the chip and see.

Because of the circuit wiring,
pin 1 is now an input on the
inside and an output on the
outside.

You can LOAD circuits you
have saved on disk into
small chips.

1. Nothing

2. Flipflop left input

3. Flipflop left output

4. Nothing

5. Nothing

6. Flipflop right input

7. Flipflop right output

8. Nothing
SHORTCUT ~

Press ESC to return to the menu.

Press ? for help or hints.

Come outside and take the chip
into the next room.
Shape Icons

Here are some special uses of
chips.

Solder pin 1 of the chip
to the INPUT of this
antenna. Notice how the
antenna pulses on and off.

This SMALL CHIP was
created by `burning"
into it a copy of the
prototype chip's circuit.

It works just like the
prototype chip, but
you can't go inside.

Solder pin 1 (upper left
pin) to the antenna INPUT.
Does it work like the
prototype chip?

Small chips are `burned"
in the Burner Room of the
INNOVATION LAB.

Go look at the Burner Room
at the left.

Look
here
{-

To burn a chip, become the
cursor and sit on the
burn button. Then press
SPACEBAR. Try it now to
see what happens.

BURN
BUTTON
 

You can make a RECORD of a
chip's circuit. You can
then review the chip
record whenever you want.

Go look at the sample Chip
Record Room at the left.

You can use small chips as
part of a circuit inside the
prototype chip. This is
called `nesting."

You can recycle small chips.
First save the old version
of the chip on a disk. Then
burn in a new circuit.

You can also SAVE a chip's
circuit on a separate disk
for later use.

To save a chip's circuit,
pick up the chip in the
INNOVATION LAB and press S.

Go try the shape editor.  Take
the crystal or sensor with you.

To load a chip, pick up
the chip and press L.
A list of circuit names
will appear.  Select the
one you want.

Chips can be loaded in
the INNOVATION LAB or in
ROBOTROPOLIS where you can
use them to help you escape.

See the manual for more
information on recording,
saving, and loading chips.
Look there for circuit
ideas, too.

You can use chips inside
robots.

Take the WALLHUGGER chip
inside this robot.

Solder the pins as shown.

1 top thruster
2 left bumper
3 left thruster
4 bottom bumper

8 top bumper
7 right thruster
6 right bumper
5 bottom thruster
PIN   TO

Take the robot to the maze
below. Close the thruster 
switch.

How does the WALLHUGGER chip
work in this kind of maze?

^ Chips can be wired inside
  other chips to create very
  complex circuits.

^ Chips can be transferred to
  ROBOTROPOLIS where you can use
  them to help you escape.

^ Chips can be used to save
  space inside a robot.

This is a PAINTBRUSH.

Use it in special rooms
of the INNOVATION LAB
to design mazes.

Try painting and erasing walls
in the maze rooms below.

Return to the Cross-
roads when you've 
finished your maze.

To paint, press SPACEBAR and
move the Paintbrush.

To erase, sit on the wall and
press SPACEBAR as you move.
PAINTBRUSH

Paintable
Maze
Rooms
  

You can use the shape editor to
change the shapes of the sensors 
and the objects they detect.

Pass a sensor or object over one
of the shape icons to change it
to that shape.

This robot will beep
when it touches an
energy crystal.  Try it.

Now, unwire the sensor
in the robot and change
its shape to a triangle.

This WALLHUGGER chip is
an example of a complex
circuit.  It is wired
with 16 logic gates and
1 nested chip.

To make or see a chip record, 
pick up a chip in the 
INNOVATION LAB and press ?

Wire it up again to make the
robot beep when it touches a
triangle.

Then return to the Crossroads.
~ To the Crossroads

examples of other
complex chips.)
Take the chip with you.

The INNOVATION LAB includes a
SHAPE EDITOR like the one
next door.

Take both chips next door to try
nesting the small chip inside
the prototype chip.

Prototype chip
goes in here.

Small chip
goes here.

Take the small chip inside the
prototype chip.  Solder its
pin 1 to the prototype's pin 1.

Next, solder a NOT-gate's OUTPUT
to the prototype's pin 3.

Put the prototype chip in
the robot and solder the
pins as shown:

Pin 1 to the antenna INPUT
Pin 3 to the left thruster

Now you have a robot that
moves right and beeps.
LEFTRIGHT PINGPONG

When you have learned 
about the Paintbrush, 
shape editor, and chips,
go this way.
CROSSROADS

By nesting chips inside
chips, you can create 
very complex circuits.

^ Chips
^ Paintbrush
^ Shape Editor

But chips can be wired inside!

You can create circuits inside
a prototype chip (using nodes,
logic gates, and flipflops) and
connect them to the pins inside.

When a chip is wired, pins
change to outputs or inputs,
depending on how they are
wired.  Unwired pins remain
neutral.

You can use a chip with a
circuit inside to activate 
robot parts.

Take the shortcut up. Bring
back the prototype chip and
the small chip.

Become the Paintbrush by picking
it up.

Look
here
{-

Disconnect the wires in the
prototype chip.

You have learned how to use many
features of the INNOVATION LAB.

Go there now and explore.
